blocks.explanation:
Yeh sawal pehli nazar mein ajeeb lagta hai, kyunke yahan sirf ek hi function \(\ln x\) hai, product (zarb) nazar nahi aata.
Diya kya hai? \(\int \ln x\,dx\). Find kya karna hai? Is ka indefinite integral.
\(\ln x\) ka integral humein yaad nahi, lekin us ka derivative \(\frac{1}{x}\) bohat aasaan hai.
Is liye chaal yeh hai: \(\ln x\) ko \(\ln x \cdot 1\) likhein, \(\ln x\) ko first aur 1 ko second function bana kar integration by parts lagayein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \ln x\,dx\), jahan \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: integration by parts, \(f(x) = \ln x\) (jis ka derivative aasaan hai) aur \(g(x) = 1\) (jis ka integral aasaan hai).

Product ki shakal banayein
\[\int \ln x\,dx = \int \ln x\cdot 1\,dx\]
Kyun: integration by parts ke formula ko do functions chahiye. 1 se zarb dene se value nahi badalti, lekin ab humare paas second function 1 aa gaya jis ka integral \(x\) hai.

Integration by parts lagayein
\[= \ln x\cdot x - \int x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\]
\[= x\ln x - \int 1\,dx\]
Kyun: pehla \(\times\) doosre ka integral \(-\) \(\int\)(doosre ka integral \(\times\) pehle ka derivative). Yahan \(\ln x \cdot x\) bana, aur andar \(x\cdot\frac{1}{x} = 1\) reh gaya, jo bilkul aasaan integral hai. Yahi is chaal ka kamaal hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\ln x\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{x}\) hai, \(\frac{1}{\ln x}\) nahi.

Integrate karein
\[= x\ln x - x + c\]
Kyun: \(\int 1\,dx = x\), aur aakhir mein ek constant \(c\) lagaya.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\ln x - x) = \ln x + x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} - 1\]
\[= \ln x\]
Kyun: \(x\ln x\) par product rule lagaya: \(1\cdot\ln x + x\cdot\frac{1}{x}\). Phir \(+1\) aur \(-1\) cancel ho gaye aur \(\ln x\) wapas mil gaya, to jawab sahi hai.
